extracted.intended_audience: regulated entities, petitioners, market participants, NASD/AMEX members, and members of the public attending federal advisory committee meetings
extracted.subtask_description: Federal Register notices setting forth procedural and substantive requirements for (a) public advisory committee meetings, (b) administrative appeals and procedural schedules, (c) securities listing/trading safeguards, (d) information collection submissions, and (e) disciplinary review procedures before self-regulatory organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public attendance and participation at ACRS meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: The entire meeting will be open to public attendance. Oral statements may be presented by members of the public with the concurrence of the Subcommittee Chairmen; written statements will be accepted and made available to the Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordings will be permitted only during those portions of the meeting open to the public, and questions may be asked only by members of the Subcommittee, its consultants, and staff. Persons desiring to make oral statements should notify the ACRS staff member named below as far in advance as is practicable so that appropriate arrangements can be made. Further information (topics, scheduling, cancellations, Chairman’s rulings on oral statements, time allotted) can be obtained by prepaid telephone call to the cognizant ACRS staff member. Persons planning to attend are urged to contact that individual one or two days before the scheduled meeting to be advised of any changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACRS meeting conduct: preliminary exchange and presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: During the initial portion of the meeting, the Subcommittees and their consultants may exchange preliminary views regarding matters to be considered during the balance of the meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Subcommittees will then hear presentations by and hold discussions with representatives of the NRC staff, their consultants, and other interested persons regarding this review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postal Rate Commission: categories of issues on appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Categories of issues apparently raised in an appeal include: (1) Effect on postal services [39 U.S.C. 404(b)(2)(C)]; (2) Effect on the community [39 U.S.C. 404(b)(2)(A)].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other legal issues may be disclosed by the record when it is filed; conversely, the determination made by the Postal Service may be found to dispose of one or more of these issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postal Rate Commission: procedural schedule and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission establishes a procedural schedule (dates for filing the record, petitions to intervene, participant statements/initial briefs, answering briefs, reply briefs, motions for oral argument) and notes the 120-day decisional schedule under 39 U.S.C. 404(b)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission reserves the right to request memoranda of law from the Postal Service on any appropriate issue; if requested, such memoranda will be due 20 days from issuance of the request and a copy shall be served on the petitioner. In briefs or motions to dismiss or affirm, the Postal Service may incorporate by reference any such memoranda previously filed. Specific schedule in the Appendix (example dates) must be followed for filing and intervention deadlines; the Commission will schedule oral argument only when necessary to the written filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visitor clearance and identification for White House advisory committee meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons attending the President’s Education Policy Advisory Committee meeting must notify the contact (Rae Nelson) no less than 24 hours before the meeting and provide, over the phone, social security number, date of birth, and name as read on driver's license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When entering the building, attendees will be required to show picture identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act: information collection submission elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency submissions to OMB for review under the Paperwork Reduction Act must include collection title, form(s) submitted, OMB number (or indication of new collection), expiration date of current OMB clearance, type of request (e.g., reinstatement), frequency of response, respondents, estimated annual number of respondents, total annual responses, average time per response, total annual reporting hours, and a collection description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of proposed forms and supporting documents should be made available from the agency clearance officer and comments should be addressed to the agency and the OMB reviewer with provided contact information and mailing addresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMEX Section 106 listing guidelines for index warrants
rubrics_metrics.description: Index warrants issues will conform to the listing guidelines under section 106 of the AMEX Company Guide: (1) the issuer of index warrants must have assets in excess of $100 million and otherwise substantially exceed the size and earning requirements in section 101(a); (2) the term of the warrants shall be for a period ranging from one to five years from the date of issuance; and (3) the minimum public distribution shall be one million warrants together with a minimum of 400 public holders, and have an aggregate market value of $4 million.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AMEX proposes to consider listing warrants on a case-by-case basis consistent with the Index Approval Order. Only substantial companies capable of meeting their warrant obligations will be eligible to issue such warrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warrant contract features and cash-settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: Nikkei warrants proposed will be direct obligations of their issuer subject to cash-settlement during their term; the AMEX intends to list both American style (exercisable throughout their life) and European style (exercisable only on expiration) warrants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon exercise (or at expiration, if not exercisable earlier), a holder of a put-type warrant receives payment to the extent the Nikkei has declined below a pre-stated cash settlement value; a call-type holder receives payment to the extent the Nikkei has increased above the pre-stated cash settlement value. Warrants that are out-of-the-money at expiration will expire worthless.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investor protection safeguards for trading Nikkei warrants
rubrics_metrics.description: Trading in Nikkei warrants will be subject to safeguards: pursuant to Commentary .02 to AMEX Rule 411, the Exchange has stated members should sell Nikkei warrants only to options-approved accounts, and the options suitability standards of AMEX Rule 923 will apply to recommended Nikkei warrant transactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Senior Registered Options Principal or Registered Options Principal is required to approve and initial a discretionary order in Nikkei warrants on the day the order is entered. Prior to commencement of trading, the AMEX will distribute a circular to its membership calling attention to the specific risks associated with warrants on the Nikkei. These suitability, disclosure, and compliance requirements are intended to address potential public customer problems arising from the derivative nature of the warrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surveillance sharing agreement requirement for foreign-index warrants
rubrics_metrics.description: Adequate surveillance sharing agreements between the AMEX and the Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE) are a necessary prerequisite to deter and detect potential manipulations or other improper or illegal trading involving the warrants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AMEX amended its surveillance sharing agreement with the TSE to include sharing market information related to the trading of Nikkei warrants. The agreement obligates both exchanges to compile and transmit market surveillance information and resolve in good faith any disagreements regarding requests for information or responses. The Commission encourages broad surveillance sharing agreements rather than product-specific agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASD: documentary evidence and witness disclosure deadline (Committee hearings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under proposed changes to Article II, the Committee staff, or the complainant, shall upon request make available to respondents and their counsel any documentary evidence and the names of any witnesses the staff intends to present at the hearing no later than five (5) business days prior to the hearing; respondents shall submit to the Committee staff or complainant any documentary evidence and names of witnesses they intend to present no later than five (5) business days prior to the hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The change would eliminate questions about whether parties were given sufficient notice of additional documentary evidence or witnesses in advance of the hearing. Notwithstanding, parties may submit additional documentary evidence at the hearing as the hearing panel, in its discretion, determines may be relevant and necessary for a complete record.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASD: evidentiary rules, counsel, and recordkeeping at hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: If a hearing is held, both the complainant and the respondent shall be entitled to be heard in person and by counsel; formal rules of evidence shall not be applicable; a record of the hearing shall be kept in all cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may submit additional documentary evidence at the hearing subject to the hearing panel's discretion to determine relevance and necessity for a complete record.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASD: Board review—time limits and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: A hearing on review by the Board shall consist of oral arguments limited to a total period of thirty (30) minutes each for argument and response by respondent and for argument and response by a complainant, unless extended by the hearing panel for good cause shown. The Board’s review shall be limited to consideration of oral arguments, written briefs, as applicable, and the record before the Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change converts Board reviews into more appellate-type proceedings and codifies practices to consider matters on the written record unless exceptional circumstances warrant otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASD: Board review—admission of additional evidence and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A party to the Board’s review may apply for leave to adduce additional evidence; such application must provide notice no later than ten (10) business days prior to the hearing, identify and describe the evidence, and demonstrate good cause for failing to adduce it before the Committee and that the evidence is material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If leave is granted, the party and opposing parties must make available to the Board hearing or review panel all documentary evidence not part of the Committee record no later than five (5) business days before the hearing. Alternatively, the Board may remand the case to the Committee for further proceedings or supplement the record on its own motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASD: treatment of appeals where the appellant did not participate before the Committee
rubrics_metrics.description: Any application for review of a matter in which the party seeking review did not participate in the proceedings before the Committee but shows good cause for the failure to participate shall normally be dismissed by the Board and remanded to the Committee for further proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the party did not show good cause, the matter shall be considered by the Board on the basis of the record before the Committee, including written briefs. A party who failed to request a hearing before the Committee will be permitted to have a hearing on review but must demonstrate good cause to adduce additional evidence. The Board may dismiss as abandoned any application for review in which the party fails to advise the Board of the basis for review or otherwise fails to provide information or a written brief in response to a request.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASD: Extended proceedings and panel composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The National Business Conduct Committee may determine, based on length of expected testimony, volume and complexity of documentary evidence, or other material factors, that a matter shall be set for an Extended Proceeding. Notice of an Extended Proceeding shall be given as provided in section 2(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All Extended Proceedings shall be held before an Extended Proceeding Committee appointed by the National Business Conduct Committee consisting of two or more persons, all of whom previously shall have served as members of the Board of Governors; however, the Chairman may appoint current Board members and compensate members at the rate then in effect for arbitrators under the Code of Arbitration Procedure.
